newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: South African wool prices fall at weekly sale.
newsitem.headline: South African wool prices fall at weekly sale.

text.p: South African wool prices fell at the latest weekly auction, the Wool Board said on Thursday.
Of the total 6,634 bales on offer, 95.6 percent was sold.
Prices for 20 micron fell 6.9 percent, 21 fell 6.0 percent, 22 lost 5.5 pct, 23 slipped 3.5 percent, 24 micron downed 5.5 percent and 25 micron slid 7.6 percent.
Bellies fell 4.0 percent, lambs fell 5.0 percent and locks rose 0.1 percent.
The offering included 1,366 bales of merino bellies, lambas and locks together with 1,016 other white, 37 bales Ciskei, 1,020 bales Lesotho and 273 bales of coarse and coloured.
Top-selling wool was 25 micron which sold 100 pct.
426 bales offered and 92.3 percent of 20 micron sold.
955 bales offered and 90.3 percent of 21 micron sold.
736 bales offered and 94.7 percent of 22 micron sold.
247 bales offered and 96.3 percent of 23 micron sold.
107 bales offered and 96.3 percent of 24 micron were sold.
The next sale will be held on February 5 with about 10,000 bales on offer.
